items.title: Ep47. How do glasses help us see better?
items.desc: In this episode, Lily and Max discover how glasses bend light to help it focus clearly inside the eye and why that can make the world look sharper. They also talk about simple habits that support healthy eyes, while learning that needing glasses isn’t something to worry about. Tune in for a bright, clear look at how our eyes and glasses work together!

items.title: Ep46. Why are there so many different animal species?
items.desc: In this episode, Lily and Max explore why there are so many different animal species. They follow the branches of the animal family tree and discover how inherited differences, changing habitats and groups becoming separated can lead to new species over many generations. Along the way, they learn that animals don’t choose to evolve and that Earth’s animal story is still unfolding.

items.title: Ep45. Why do we get goosebumps?
items.desc: In this episode, Lily and Max explore why we get goosebumps when we’re cold, frightened, excited, or moved by music. They discover how tiny muscles pull hairs upright, why this reaction may have helped our furry ancestors, and where the name “goosebumps” comes from.

items.title: Ep44. How many bananas would make a monkey sick?
items.desc: In this playful episode of Little Ears, Big Ideas, Max and Lily explore whether monkeys can eat too many bananas. Kids learn that even healthy foods can be a problem in huge amounts, and that wild monkeys actually eat lots of different foods, not just bananas. A fun, silly question turns into a gentle lesson about balance, bodies, and what animals really eat.

items.title: Ep43. Whoosh! What makes wind?
items.desc: In this episode, Lily and Max follow the clues to discover what makes wind. They explore how differences in air pressure get air moving, why wind can change speed and direction, and how thunderstorms can bring sudden gusts. Plus, Max learns what a “southerly” really means and finds out that even a paper windmill can help us spot the wind!
